findings.finding: --parent-sha interpolated unquoted in the format() output, unlike sibling gates' quoted --head-sha "${{ github.sha }}"; not exploitable (github.event.before is always a 40-hex SHA or all-zeros sentinel, both tested fail-open paths) but an avoidable inconsistency.
findings.suggestion: fixed: format() template now quotes the SHA value (--parent-sha "{0}"), matching sibling steps' convention; shape test and docstring updated to match; ci_supplychain_ack.json regenerated for the new fingerprint.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: The auxiliary growth signal fails OPEN on any infra fault and must never turn an infra hiccup into a red main. — It used raw subprocess.run(text=True) for git show <parent>:<path> and git rev-parse, regressing a defect class (MAX_PATH trap, absent-vs-broken conflation) already fixed elsewhere via git_blob_read.py, and could raise an uncaught UnicodeDecodeError on a non-UTF-8 parent baseline, escaping to EXIT_INFRA -- indistinguishable from EXIT_BLOCKED at the CI shell-exit-code level.
findings.suggestion: fixed: rewrote the parent-blob read to go through git_blob_read.blob_oid (separates absent from broken) and git_helpers._run_git (errors="ignore", never raises) instead of raw subprocess calls. Added two tests covering both branches.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: A --write that adds a newly-unbound AC to the baseline anywhere within the pushed commit range is CLOSED. — The push-triggered run is a one-shot, self-clearing detective signal, not a required PR check -- it self-clears the following push once the grown entry is inside every later before SHA, leaving no trace if a maintainer misses the one red run.
findings.suggestion: fixed: softened docstring, ci.yml comment, docs/hooks-and-pipeline.md, the decision-drop, and the changelog bullet to describe this as "surfaced, not durably closed" / detective / self-clearing, rather than CLOSED.

findings.finding: A force-push to `main` (which the docstring itself notes the solo-maintainer `--admin` path can take) makes `github.event.before` a commit that is no longer reachable from any ref; on a fresh runner with `fetch-depth: 0`, the fetch of the rewritten `main` does not download that commit, `rev-parse --verify` fails, and the growth check fails open — the push goes green with only a log warning. So a maintainer force-push carrying a self-grandfathering baseline edit is a silent bypass. This is consistent with the module's documented fail-open contract for the auxiliary signal, so it's a disclosed design limit rather than a bug — but it's not called out in the "what this does not close" prose, which is otherwise exhaustive.
findings.suggestion: Add one sentence to the docstring / docs paragraph acknowledging force-push-to-`main` as a fail-open path, or have CI escalate an unresolvable `before` on a non-new branch to a hard failure (it's distinguishable from the all-zeros new-branch case because the ref already existed).

findings.finding: The parent-baseline shape check rejects a doc that lacks a string-list `unbound`, but the current baseline file format includes `schema_version` (the unit tests write it, the CLI's own baseline presumably does too). A parent baseline that is valid JSON with the right `unbound` list but a different `schema_version` than the current reader understands is silently accepted — the growth diff compares raw string sets across what may be different schema generations. Given the shape check exists precisely to distrust the parent blob, this is a minor asymmetry.
findings.suggestion: Either also require/compare `schema_version` on the parent blob, or note that string-set diffing is intentionally schema-agnostic.

findings.finding: The test asserts the exact `format(...)` expression substring, which is strong, but nothing pins the two halves of the `if:` and the `run:` flag condition to agree — a regression that flipped the `run` condition to `github.event_name == 'pull_request' && ...` while keeping the widened `if:` would pass every assertion here (the exact-expression substring still matches; the trigger tests still pass) while making the push trigger a no-op signal. The step would run on push with no growth check — exactly the round-1 overclaim this iterate exists to prevent.
findings.suggestion: Add an assertion tying the two together, e.g. that the `run` expression contains `github.event_name == 'push'` (it does implicitly via the exact substring — actually the exact substring already contains `github.event_name == 'push' &&`, so this is covered). On re-inspection this is adequately pinned; disregard unless the substring is ever relaxed.  (I retracted the third finding on closer reading — the exact-substring assertion already encodes `push &&`; I leave the reasoning visible so the reviewer trail stays honest.)  No correctness bugs found in `_ac_baseline_growth.py` (argument-list subprocess, no shell; ValueError on `relative_to` handled; bootstrap-vs-fault distinction correct; `--write` + growth combination rejected at the parser). No injection risk: `github.event.before` is a 40-hex SHA on push events and is passed unquoted into the shell run line, which is fine for that value shape. No regressions: the pull_request payload shape is unchanged (key omitted without the flag, tested), `_run_gate`'s new parameters are defaulted, and the sibling gates' `if:` conditions are pinned by a dedicated test.  Overall: ship-as-is — the two findings are documentation-of-limits refinements on an already well-disclosed fail-open auxiliary signal, not defects in the mechanism itself.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: approve
